content: Cefadroxil, marketed under the brand name DURICEF, is a semisynthetic cephalosporin antibiotic formulated for oral administration. It appears as a white to yellowish-white crystalline powder. This compound is water-soluble and stable in acidic environments. Chemically, it is designated as 5-Thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylic acid, 7-amino-3-methyl-8-oxo-, monohydrate. The structural formula of DURICEF is provided in its documentation. The 1 g film-coated DURICEF tablets include the following inactive ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, magnesium stearate, polyethylene glycol, polysorbate 80, simethicone emulsion, and titanium dioxide. The DURICEF oral suspension contains the following inactive ingredients: FD&C Yellow No. 6, natural and artificial flavors, polysorbate 80, sodium benzoate, sucrose, and xanthan gum. DURICEF capsules are composed of the following inactive ingredients: D&C Red No. 28, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Red No. 40, gelatin, magnesium stearate, and titanium dioxide.
